_notes: UI-005 — the Notification module actually delivers email (plan test-plans/system/notification-email.md, runner row UI-005). notify-now returns a per-recipient outcome (success / failed / skipped) carrying the transport's own error, so a broken mail configuration fails the build instead of dropping messages silently — there is no outbox table anywhere in the product. The job result is the assertion; a message landing in a mailbox is a side effect for eyeballing, never what passes or fails the test.

Not the clock-out notification (B12-R10): that path takes the process-wide sender chosen from the API's environment at startup, which no test can configure, and reports nothing. This one resolves SMTP from database preferences, which is why it is reachable.

Mail settings are written when the deployment has none — the product stores this password in clear text and cannot be given an encrypted one; encryption is a later phase. Writing beats demanding: dev resets wipe the preferences and a check-only run would leave CI red until someone re-ran a manual setup. NOTIFY_SMTP_WRITE=0 makes the run read-only (environment, read by the flow, not data).

recipientTag: the recipient is EMAIL_TO's first address — the same one the framework's own reporter would mail, never a committed literal — plus-addressed per run as +ui005-<clock>. A user is soft-deleted, never purged, and its email stays reserved, so reusing EMAIL_TO verbatim meant the second run ever got 409 userEmailInUse at create and this test could pass exactly once per address. The tag routes to the same mailbox, so a human can still eyeball the mail.

notificationNamePrefix must be the residue sweep's uid prefix for notifications (cleanupTargets.ts); the flow appends uid(), which carries the full clock so the sweep can date a leftover. subjectTemplate's {stamp} is a short clock stamp from src/data/generated.

The filter script has to produce a report: dispatch renders one and attaches it, so a script with executeReport=false comes back failed / 'render failed' with nothing sent. Dev returns exactly such a row (DashBoardTimeInReviewOfCrewProductivity) FIRST, which is what made taking scripts[0] fail — the flow takes the first REPORTING script; the content is not asserted, only that there is something to render.

expected: the job settles complete and reports exactly one recipient whose status is success, zero failed, at least one successful. cleanup: the notification first (it references the user), then the user — both by the minted names.
